title: How can two waves smaller than a half circle be identical?
description: Two waves smaller than a half circle are drawn on a central line of twelve centimetres, one above the line and one below it. The video picks one opening and one tip distance for both waves, then checks that they match with a ruler.
teaching_notes: One idea: identical waves come from one opening and one tip distance, with the tip off the line on the opposite side from the wave. Watch for children who put the tip on the line, which gives a half circle.

source: Try to recreate the figure where the waves are smaller than a half circle (as appearing in the neck of the figure 'A Person'). The challenge here is to get both the waves to be identical. This may be tricky!
video_script.why: The child uses the off-the-line tip of the person to draw two identical arcs, one above and one below a central line.
video_script.substitution: A central line of twelve centimetres, two waves on six centimetres each, opening five centimetres and tips four centimetres from the line.
video_script.anchor: Two waves smaller than a half circle on a central line, as in the neck of the person
video_script.payoff_line: Both waves use the same opening and the same tip distance, so they are identical.

final_answer.value: open ended; two identical arcs of the same radius on equal lengths of the line, one above the line and one below it, each smaller than a half circle (for 6 cm of line each: opening 5 cm, tips 4 cm from the line, each arc 1 cm high)
final_answer.spoken: both waves use the same opening and the same tip distance, so they are identical; with six centimetres of line for each wave, the opening is five centimetres and the tips are four centimetres from the line

never_show: the finished waves before the answer
maths_rules: AB = 12 cm; X is halfway, so AX = XB = 12 / 2 = 6 cm.
Half of 6 cm is 6 / 2 = 3 cm; the opening must be bigger than 3 cm, so take 5 cm.

First wave: tip 4 cm below the line, straight below the middle of AX (3 cm from A); each end of the wave is 5 cm from the tip (3-4-5 right triangle, checked with a ruler); the arc above the line is 5 - 4 = 1 cm high.
Second wave: tip 4 cm above the line, straight above the middle of XB (9 cm from A), the same opening 5 cm; the arc below the line is 1 cm deep.
Check: same opening 5 cm and same tip distance 4 cm, so both waves are 1 cm high and identical.
video_script.design: One idea: one opening and one tip distance make two identical arcs. Uses the off-the-line tip of the person. The line AB stays all video.
